subtopic: Caring for ageing parents while working
subtype: Approach: building in rest and respite for the caregiver [Thinking]
passage: Sit down, beta. I am Alka, and I will tell you something I learned at twenty-six, when I was looking after my mother and holding down a job. For months I ran on nothing. One evening I fell asleep at the dining table with the spoon in my hand and thought: if I break, who does the caring? It is not a sprint. It is more like a long journey, and you must plan where you will rest. So I told my brother Francis, "Every Thursday evening is mine. Please be here from six." He did not argue. On Thursdays I walked, or sat with a friend, or did nothing at all. Amma was well looked after, and I had energy again the next day. That one evening off is what kept the rest going.

qa.q: Which evening did Alka ask Francis to cover?
What was Alka feeling on the evening she fell asleep at the table?
qa.a: Alka felt alarm and fear of breaking down, shown by wondering who would do the caring if that happened.

qa.q: What choice did Alka make that changed things, and why did it work?
qa.a: Alka asked Francis to cover Thursday evenings so that rest was built in, and the regular rest brought back the energy to keep caring.

qa.q: How might Francis have felt when Alka asked?
qa.a: Francis may have felt glad to be given a clear, doable role, since he did not argue.

grounding: Alka recalls scheduling a weekly evening off, covered by Francis, as part of planning care for the long run.
